items.title: 66096_Monk Montgomery oral history interview
items.q: And when I went to Seattle to work, to play with Elmer, it worked out fine. Elmer had a trio, which was piano, guitar and electric bass.

ctx.x: It was still a gimmick, but kind of like the awareness of it was happening. There was country-western players and different guys was...not just in jazz. The electric bass was a sound that people were getting just a little more accustomed to, turned on about.

And when I went to Seattle to work, to play with Elmer, it worked out fine. Elmer had a trio, which was piano, guitar and electric bass. So just because mine was more a -- well, I just keep using the word gimmick -- novelty, I got a lot of attention. Elmer gave me a lot of solos; I got a lot of playing in. I got a lot of playing in.

In the meantime, by the consistency of playing, the length of time in Indianapolis and before, I still had good chops. After I worked with Elmer, and it wasn't a long period, I was a little bit unhappy because that wasn't the way I wanted to play.
